test_title: PYST 39: RRB Group D - GA (Held On: 14 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: What does the Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025, prohibit unless female heirs receive their inheritance first?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Dedication to Waqf**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025** (introduced as the **Waqf (Amendment) Bill, 2024**) introduces significant reforms to the **Waqf Act, 1995**, specifically targeting the protection of **inheritance rights**.
 
• Under the new provisions, the **dedication of property to Waqf** is prohibited if such a dedication results in the deprivation of the **legal heirs**, especially **female heirs**, of their rightful **inheritance**.
 
• This amendment seeks to ensure that religious endowments do not become a tool to bypass the **succession rights** of women as guaranteed under **personal laws** or other legal frameworks. ***Hence, the statement regarding the prohibition of dedication is correct.***
 
• The Act mandates that any person intending to dedicate property as **Waqf** must have a **clear title** and ownership of the property, and they must be a **practicing Muslim** for at least **five years**.
 
• The legislation aims to bring **transparency** and **accountability** to the management of over **9 lakh hectares** of Waqf land across India, which is currently managed by various **State Waqf Boards**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Waqf Definition and Purpose**:
 
 
• **Waqf** refers to the permanent **dedication of movable or immovable property** for purposes recognized by **Muslim Law** as pious, religious, or charitable.
 
• Properties dedicated to Waqf are managed by a **Mutawalli** (manager), who acts as a supervisor rather than an owner.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Central Waqf Council**:
 
 
• The **Central Waqf Council** is a **statutory body** established in **1964** to advise the **Union Government** on matters concerning the working of **Waqf Boards**.
 
• The **2025 Amendment** proposes a more diverse composition of the Council, including the mandatory inclusion of **two women** and **two non-Muslims** to enhance inclusivity and administrative oversight.
 
 
 
• **Powers of the District Collector**:
 
 
• One of the most debated features of the **Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025** is the enhanced power given to the **District Collector**.
 
• The **Collector** now has the authority to determine whether a property claimed as **Waqf** is actually **government land**. This shifts the adjudicatory power away from the **Waqf Tribunal** in cases of land title disputes involving the state.
 
 
 
• **Registration and Portal**:
 
 
• The Act introduces a **centralized registration** process through a global **Waqf portal** to digitize records and prevent **encroachments**.
 
• Any property intended to be declared as **Waqf-alal-aulad** (Waqf for the benefit of the dedicator's family) must also ensure that the **inheritance rights** of **female heirs** are not compromised.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Abolition of 'Waqf by User'**: The **Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025** seeks to abolish the concept of **'Waqf by User'**, where a property is deemed Waqf based on long-term religious use without formal documentation. This necessitates formal **registration** for all Waqf properties.
 
• **Composition of State Waqf Boards**: The boards will now include members from diverse backgrounds, including **Shia, Sunni, Bohra, and Agakhani** communities, alongside **two non-Muslim members** and at least **two women**.
 
• **Timeline**: The **Waqf Act** was originally enacted in **1954**, significantly amended in **1995** and **2013**, and the current **2025** reforms represent the most comprehensive shift in **Waqf administration** since Independence.
